title: Per-Trace Agent Cost from Model Pricing
dataSources: Token counts on LLM spans (`num_input_tokens`, `num_output_tokens`, `total_tokens`) and the org Model Pricing table
description: Shows what each agent request cost by multiplying the token counts on its LLM spans by the org Model Pricing table in Splunk Agent Observability, and keeps that table current.
value: Per-request cost tells the team which prompts, tools or models are expensive, which is where optimisation pays off. A stale price table makes every figure wrong.
implementation: Log `model` and token counts on every LLM span. Ask an admin to add a Model Pricing row for each model string the agents use, and review prices when the provider changes them. New prices apply to new traces only.
visualization: Cost column in the Agent Stream trace table.
knownFalsePositives: Historical traces keep the old price after a change. The documentation does not say what an unpriced model displays; when a model shows 0.0, report its token counts instead.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The agent is already instrumented as described in UC-13.8.1: every request is a trace with at least one agent span, LLM spans carry `model`, token counts and the `tools` schemas, and tool spans carry `name`, `duration_ns` and `tool_call_id`. The `model` string must match the Model Pricing row exactly. OpenTelemetry ingest uses `gen_ai.usage.*` instead of the SDK token fields.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Admins open the org Model Pricing table and add or update a row per model string.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare the cost of one trace with its token counts times the listed price. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Review Model Pricing when a provider changes prices or the agents adopt a new model.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Cost shows 0.0 or nothing: the model string has no row, or token counts are missing on the LLM span.
grandmaExplanation: We work out what each answer cost from how many words the assistant read and wrote, using a price list that we keep up to date.

productArtifacts.title: Model Pricing maintenance
productArtifacts.body:
Where: org Model Pricing table (admins edit it)
Rows: one per model string logged on LLM spans
Formula: per-trace cost = LLM span token counts x Model Pricing for that model
Change rule: new prices apply to new traces only; historical traces keep the old price
Separate: evaluator spend is on the Integration Costs page; SaaS billing to Splunk (spans ingested, Luna tokens) is a third number. Do not add them together.
